chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Isa ibn al-Qasim said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the visitation (of the Prophet's shrine) after the pilgrimage in the days of Tashriq, and he said: 'No.' He added: 'It does not contradict the first report, because the meaning in this report is that we should understand it as indicating preference and recommendation, rather than prohibition.'

key_terms.التَّشْرِيق: The days of Tashriq (11th-13th of Dhu al-Hijjah) following Eid al-Adha
key_terms.الزِّيَارَة: Visitation (specifically of the Prophet or Imams)
key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَاب: Recommendation (a legal ruling indicating merit but not obligation)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to visit the Prophet's shrine in Medina during the days of Tashriq after Hajj?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ruling on performing voluntary circumambulation (Tawaf al-Nafila) in Mecca during the Days of Tashriq. He resolves apparent contradictions in reports by interpreting restrictions as recommendations against it (istihbab) rather than strict prohibitions (haram), allowing pilgrims to visit the Prophet's shrine in Medina during this period. This reflects the Shia scholarly principle of harmonizing narrations by distinguishing between absolute prohibition and preferred abstention.
